title: Natural zigzags of inverse functors give homotopy equivalent nerves
statement: Let $\mathcal A,\mathcal B$ be small categories. Use the ordinary nerve, its geometric realization, and weak homotopy equivalence conventions of [def-coef-zigzag-homotopy-calculus]. For functors $F,G:\mathcal A\to\mathcal B$, a natural transformation $\eta:F\Rightarrow G$ is a family $\eta_a:F(a)\to G(a)$ with $G(t)\eta_a=\eta_{a'}F(t)$ for every $t:a\to a'$. Such a transformation induces a continuous homotopy $|NF|\simeq|NG|$. Consequently, suppose $P:\mathcal A\to\mathcal B$ and $Q:\mathcal B\to\mathcal A$ are functors and there are finite zigzags of natural transformations, with either orientation allowed at each link, from $QP$ to $\mathrm{id}_{\mathcal A}$ and from $PQ$ to $\mathrm{id}_{\mathcal B}$. Then $|NP|$ and $|NQ|$ are inverse up to continuous homotopy. In particular $NP:N\mathcal A\to N\mathcal B$ is a weak homotopy equivalence. No component of the natural transformations is required to be an isomorphism.

source.place: Proposition 8.2, following Proofs paragraph (ii), printed p. 29 (PDF page 13): natural transformations induce homotopies between nerves; the inverse-functor consequence is obtained by concatenating these homotopies. No Stacks tag is claimed.

proof.text: Construct $T:\mathcal A\times[1]\to\mathcal B$, where $[1]$ has objects $0,1$ and one nonidentity arrow $0\to1$. On objects set $T(a,0)=F(a)$, $T(a,1)=G(a)$; on arrows $t:a\to a'$ at constant level use $F(t)$ or $G(t)$, and on a mixed arrow use $G(t)\eta_a=\eta_{a'}F(t)$. Naturality is precisely the equality between these two expressions. Identities follow from those of $F,G$. In a composable pair there can be at most one mixed arrow: the cases $0,0,1$ and $0,1,1$ reduce respectively to this naturality equation and functoriality of $G$; constant-level pairs use functoriality of $F$ or $G$. Thus $T$ is a functor. In degree $n$ a functor $[n]\to\mathcal A\times[1]$ is exactly a pair of functors into the two factors, and $N[1]_n=\operatorname{Hom}_{\Delta}([n],[1])$. The ordinary nerve definition in [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones] therefore gives a simplicial map $NT:N\mathcal A\times\Delta^1\to N\mathcal B$ with endpoint restrictions $NF,NG$.

source.place: Proposition 8.2, Proofs paragraph (ii), printed p. 29; agent expansion of the interval-category construction

proof.text:
Write a simplex of $N\mathcal A$ as $\sigma=(a_0\to\cdots\to a_n)$, with barycentric coordinates $\lambda_j\geq0$, $\sum_j\lambda_j=1$. Put $S_i=\sum_{j=i}^n\lambda_j$, $S_{n+1}=0$. The closed sets $R_i=\{(\lambda,t):S_{i+1}\leq t\leq S_i\}$, $0\leq i\leq n$, cover $|\Delta^n|\times[0,1]$. On $R_i$ use the simplex
$$F(a_0)\to\cdots\to F(a_i)\xrightarrow{\eta_{a_i}}G(a_i)\to\cdots\to G(a_n)$$
with weights
$$(\lambda_0,\ldots,\lambda_{i-1},S_i-t,t-S_{i+1},\lambda_{i+1},\ldots,\lambda_n).$$
The weights are nonnegative and sum to one. This gives a continuous map on each $R_i$ into the quotient realization of [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones]. At the common boundary $t=S_i$, the two neighboring formulas delete respectively $F(a_i)$ and $G(a_{i-1})$; their remaining mixed arrow is the same because $\eta_{a_i}F(a_{i-1}\to a_i)=G(a_{i-1}\to a_i)\eta_{a_{i-1}}$. Nonneighboring overlaps only insert additional zero weights, so the same successive deletions give equality there. The maps glue continuously on the whole prism: for a closed subset of the target its preimage is a finite union of sets closed in the closed $R_i$, hence closed in the prism. This verifies the finite closed pasting argument directly.

source.place: Proposition 8.2, Proofs paragraph (ii), printed p. 29; agent barycentric prism construction

proof.text: These prism maps descend through the realization identifications in [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones]. A face sets one $\lambda_j$ to zero: removing that vertex composes the adjacent arrows, and if it meets the mixed arrow the two composites agree by the naturality equation of step 1. In the formula of step 2 the corresponding cumulative sums are repeated, so the zero-width region is deleted and every remaining weight is the lower-dimensional weight. A degeneracy repeats one vertex: its arrow is an identity, its two adjacent weights add, and the cumulative-sum formula then gives the formula for the original simplex. If the cut lies between the repeats, the two identical vertices at one level merge and the sole remaining mixed arrow is the same $\eta_a$. Thus faces and degeneracies, which generate all realization relations, are respected. Let $q:\coprod_{n,\sigma\in N\mathcal A_n}|\Delta^n|\to|N\mathcal A|$ be the defining quotient map. Apply [lem-cbc-quotient-cylinder-continuity] with this $q$ and the usual interval $[0,1]$, whose neighborhoods contain compact closed subinterval neighborhoods. The pullback of the descended map along $q\times1$ is continuous on every summand by step 2, so the descended $H_\eta:|N\mathcal A|\times[0,1]\to|N\mathcal B|$ is continuous. At $t=0$ all $G$ weights vanish and at $t=1$ all $F$ weights vanish. Hence its endpoints are exactly $|NF|,|NG|$. No inverse to any $\eta_a$ has been used.

source.place: Proposition 8.2, Proofs paragraph (ii), printed p. 29; agent verification of descent and joint continuity

proof.text: For each link of the finite zigzag from $QP$ to $\mathrm{id}_{\mathcal A}$ take the homotopy of step 3; for a reversed link replace its time parameter by $1-t$. If there are $r>0$ links, on $[j/r,(j+1)/r]$ use the $j$th homotopy at time $rt-j$. The formulas agree at subdivision endpoints, so the same finite closed pasting argument used in step 2 proves continuity. For $r=0$ use the constant homotopy. Repeat for the zigzag from $PQ$ to $\mathrm{id}_{\mathcal B}$. Applying functors to composable chains and the same barycentric coordinates shows directly from [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones] that $|N(QP)|=|NQ|\circ|NP|$, $|N(PQ)|=|NP|\circ|NQ|$, and the realized identity functors are identity maps. Consequently the two concatenations are homotopies $|NQ|\circ|NP|\simeq1$ and $|NP|\circ|NQ|\simeq1$.

source.place: Proposition 8.2, following Proofs paragraph (ii), printed p. 29; finite zigzag consequence

proof.text: Set $X=|N\mathcal A|$, $Y=|N\mathcal B|$, $f=|NP|$, and $g=|NQ|$. Step 4 supplies the two continuous homotopies required by [lem-coef-homotopy-equivalence-weak]. That statement gives a bijection on path components and an isomorphism $\pi_n(X,x)\to\pi_n(Y,f(x))$ for every $n\geq1$ and every $x\in X$, without assuming the homotopies fix basepoints. These are exactly the weak-homotopy-equivalence conditions of [def-coef-zigzag-homotopy-calculus]. Therefore $NP$ is a weak homotopy equivalence, and step 4 already gives the asserted continuous homotopy inverses.
